To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) vertebral patterning in the chick embryo involves a resegmentation‐based mechanism in which the sclerotome repositions itself with respect to the adjacent myotome; (2) the mechanism varies along the vertebral axis; (3) the shift is dependent on the position of cells within the sclerotome; and (4) the shift is mediated by a combination of signals, including Wnts.
(1) somite contributions to vertebrae are not always restricted to the half‐somite from which they are derived and that (2) somite contribution patterns are not uniform along the vertebral axis.

how the body plan is established during embryogenesis.
the development of the vertebrate skeleton and in particular, the patterning of vertebrae in the chick embryo.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the sclerotomal cells of a single somite contribute to two successive vertebrae in the amniotes, but that these vertebrae are formed by the resegmentation of two adjacent somites, except for those cells in the sclerotome that are positioned in the ventromedial half of the segment, which shift to the adjacent somite.

(a) sclerotome is made from the ventral half of the somite; (b) sclerotome shifts in a region‐dependent manner; (c) resegmentation is a mechanism of vertebra formation; and (d) vertebra formation involves a combination of region‐specific resegmentation and region‐specific sclerotome shifts.
the vertebral bodies are formed by resegmentation, while the neural arches and ribs are formed by a shift mechanism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
vertebral bodies form by resegmenting sclerotome cells, whereas neural arches form from a single somitic sclerotome, but that the sclerotomes shift in a region specific manner.
the sclerotomal contribution to the vertebra comes from a single somitic segment, whereas the neural arch contribution comes from two somites.
vertebral patterning in chick is a combination of the resegmentation and shift mechanisms, with the shift mechanism occurring in a region‐ and cell‐specific manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mechanism of vertebral patterning is not a single, simple process.
the mechanism of vertebral patterning is more complex than previously believed.
there are two mechanisms of vertebral patterning: resegmentation, in which two somites are combined to make a vertebra, and somite‐shift, in which a single somite is shifted to make a vertebra.
